# Lit panel: per-cell full-profile imputation when each sample measures one exploratory marker on a shared backbone (N079)

Literature tools worked (WebSearch + WebFetch + Europe PMC full text). The quotes are verbatim: full-text greps (Europe PMC XML) or
abstracts (Europe PMC API) where marked [FT]/[ABS]; quotes marked [WF] come from WebFetch extraction (the extractor caps quotes at
about 125 characters).

## Mapping to BSCCM
Infinity Flow: backbone = about 14 shared antibodies in every well, plus 1 exploratory PE antibody per well, with one regressor per
exploratory marker. BSCCM: backbone = 24 LED-array channels (the image), plus 1 single-stain marker per slide, plus 4 pooled
channels on 'all' slides. In both, no cell has two exploratory markers measured. The structure is the same; our "backbone" is an
image representation, not antibodies.

## (1) Model classes
- **Infinity Flow (Becht 2021, Sci Adv; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8457665/)**
  - Per-marker regressors on the backbone: "One regression model per algorithm and Infinity antibody is fit." [WF]
  - Algorithms: XGBoost, SVM, NN (keras), and LASSO on polynomials. "XGBoost was more accurate than other nonlinear models for
    virtually any marker-algorithm pair" [FT].
  - Linear models do much worse: "linear model performed much worse (median AUC of 0.71)" vs nonlinear "median AUC between 0.88
    and 0.89" [WF].
- **pyInfinityFlow (Ferchen 2023, Bioinformatics; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10166583/)**: also XGBoost.
  "impute new surface markers into an existing flow cytometry backbone panel using XGBoost regression" [WF]
- **kNN / copy-from-neighbours panel merging**
  - CyTOFmerge (Abdelaal 2019; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6792069/): "imputed by taking the median values of those
    markers from the k-most-similar cells", with k = 50 best [WF].
  - CytoBackBone (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6792066/): "based on nearest-neighbor imputation, but introduces the
    notion of acceptable and non-ambiguous nearest neighbors" [ABS].
  - cyCombine (Pedersen 2022, Nat Commun; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8971492/): SOM clusters on the shared markers,
    then a "multi-dimensional kernel density estimate" draw [WF].
- **Joint latent (multi-output) models**
  - CytoVI (Ingelfinger et al., bioRxiv Sep 2025; https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2025.09.07.674699.full): a totalVI-style
    mask; the encoder sees the shared markers and "the generative network reconstructs the union of all markers present in the
    antibody panels" [WF].
  - CyStainer (Ivanov et al., bioRxiv 30 Jun 2026; https://sciety.org/articles/activity/10.64898/2026.06.30.735235): a transformer
    VAE that imputes "without a set of shared backbone markers" and is benchmarked on InfinityFlow data. Only the abstract is
    available, with no numbers.

## (2) How joint / co-expression correctness is validated; accuracy; failure modes
- **Infinity Flow**
  - Validation is per marker on held-out cells of the same well: "randomly split into a training set (50% of the events)" [WF].
    The metric is AUC against manual gates, "within a range of AUC from 0.72 to 0.98" [WF].
  - Cross-well generalisation is tested by treating backbone markers as fake exploratory markers: "rotating out Backbone markers
    one at a time and using the remaining Backbone markers to predict the intensity of the left-out marker... (median Δ R 2 from
    −0.015 to −0.012)" [FT].
  - Joint co-expression was checked only with a NEW wet experiment: "Staining with these markers in an independent flow cytometry
    experiment validated the predicted coexpression patterns for these markers (fig. S10)" [FT].
  - Failure modes:
    - "The expression of an Infinity marker requires a unique signature in the Backbone data to be accurately imputed. A TCR Vβ7 +
      T cell, however, resembles any other T cell" [FT]
    - "Markers restricted to rare cell populations, in general, gave lower AUC values" [FT]
    - "predictions include a significant and underdispersed contribution from nonspecific signal" [FT]
    - "the Backbone is an information bottleneck in MPC assays" [FT]
- **Mocking et al. 2023 (Cytometry A 103:818; DOI 10.1002/cyto.a.24774)**
  - An independent benchmark of Infinicyt, CyTOFmerge, CytoBackBone and cyCombine on split panels with known truth [ABS]:
    "CyTOFmerge showed the most accurate approximation ... with a mean F-score between 0.53 and 0.87 when retrieving cell
    populations"; "Performance remained inadequate for all methods, with only limited similarity at the cell level."
  - This is the clearest statement of the "cluster-level correct, cell-level not" failure.
- **CyTOFmerge**
  - Validated at the population level: "imputed expression profiles of the 121 populations are remarkably similar (average
    correlation of 0.998)" and "adjusted Rand-index of 0.81" [WF].
  - Per-cell correlation was dropped: "this approach turned out not to be appropriate for our data" [WF].
  - Accuracy depends on how many backbone dimensions are informative: "performances improve when the number of shared markers
    increases ... saturate at m = 16" [WF].
- **cyCombine**: "imputed marker expressions should generally only be used for visualization purposes" and "we do not recommend
  basing differential expression analyses directly on imputed values" [WF].
- **CytoVI**
  - Uses semi-synthetic held-out markers: "Lineage markers such as CD4, CD14 or CD3 were imputed with high accuracy (Pearson's r >
    0.9), while Ki67 or CD103 achieved lower imputation results" [WF].
  - Its uncertainty "strongly correlated with the" imputation error [WF].
- **Over-correlation failure (joint model)**: HistoPlexer (Nat Mach Intell 2025; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12364712/)
  - Validates co-expression with marker-pair Spearman correlations of prediction vs truth.
  - "for some protein pairs (for example, CD3:CD8a and CD20:CD3), the SCC in MP exceeds that of the GT ... overestimated
    co-localization patterns" [FT].
- **Bottom line for (2)**
  - No paper validates joint correctness against truly co-measured exploratory markers at scale. The checks used are:
    - held-out cells of the same well (marginal only);
    - leave-one-backbone-marker-out;
    - population or gating F-score;
    - small wet-lab co-stains.
  - Reported cell-level accuracy is modest and depends on the marker.
  - The dominant failure is that accuracy is set by the backbone: imputation is cluster-level, and markers without a backbone
    signature (or on rare cells) fail.

## (3) Do joint (multi-output) models beat per-marker regressors?
- **For: HistoPlexer (H&E→IMC, all markers co-measured in training).**
  - "The MP setting consistently outperforms SP across all methods" [FT].
  - "The MP model achieves an MSE approximately an order of magnitude lower than that of the SP model" on marker-pair correlations [FT].
  - Mechanism: "learning intermarker correlations ... and leveraging auxiliary morphological information from abundant markers" [FT].
  - Caveat: it needs co-measured targets, which BSCCM does not have.
- **Against or neutral**
  - CITE-seq protein-imputation benchmark (Li et al., Genome Biol 2025-03; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11881419/):
    across 12 methods, "Seurat v4 (PCA) and Seurat v3 (PCA) demonstrate exceptional performance" [ABS]. These are kNN/anchor
    transfer methods, which beat the deep joint models (totalVI, sciPENN) [ABS].
  - The Mocking benchmark winner is kNN (CyTOFmerge).
  - CytoVI beats only cyCombine and kNN, not per-marker XGBoost [WF; comparison absent].
- **Transfer evidence for shared trunks**: in silico labeling (Christiansen 2018, Cell;
  https://research.google/blog/seeing-more-with-in-silico-labeling-of-microscopy-images/): "new labels can be learned with
  minimal additional training data" [WF].
- **Project check**: the project's own joint head (N062 panel-matrix latent) was flat. Pooled outputs gained .015 to .031, bought
  with -.01 to -.02 on singles. This is consistent with the literature: joint heads add nothing without co-measured targets.

## (4) Label-free image backbones
- **Reflectance microscopy (bioRxiv 2020.07.31.231613; https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2020.07.31.231613v1.full)**
  - Per-marker networks: "multiple DL models are independently trained for individual IF labels".
  - Single-stain batches are combined: "digital multiplexing by feeding the same reflectance input to each network" [WF].
  - This is the BSCCM design. The combined predictions were not validated against co-stains beyond one Hoechst/EdU pair [WF].
- **DeepIFC (Timonen 2023, Cytometry A; DOI 10.1002/cyto.a.24770)**: BF/DF → fluorescence images; types cells by thresholding the
  predicted channels. "rarer cell types are predicted well when a balanced data set is used to train the model" [ABS].
- **Nazir & Behera, arXiv 2605.14717 (May 2026, ICPR 2026; BSCCM)**: a multi-task model (WBC class + protein regression) on DPC.
  "a 0.72 Pearson correlation for CD16 expression regression on BSCCM" [WF]. No joint/co-expression validation and no
  single-task ablation on the abstract page.
- **Not found**: no 2025-26 paper decodes a joint multi-marker profile from single-stain label-free data with a co-expression
  validation. CyStainer (2026) is the closest, but it works on cytometry and not on images.

## Ideas for BSCCM (declined.md respected: no exclusivity/lineage priors in training; validation checks only)

**A. Joint-correctness card (Mocking / HistoPlexer style).**
- Mechanism: on held-out 'all'-slide cells, compare three things between the measured pooled channels and the composed predictions:
  - the 4x4 correlation matrix (HistoPlexer pair-SCC MSE; detects over-correlation from regression to type means);
  - a within-type-gate correlation (cell-level vs cluster-level; N022 within-class r was only .15 to .22);
  - gating F-score (Mocking; F1 of populations from predicted vs measured gates).
- Add ensemble-variance vs |error| calibration (CytoVI) and exclusive-pair double-positive rates as checks only.
- Why it helps joint decoding: N079 showed per-channel composition r of .778. It did not show whether pairwise structure and
  within-type variation are right, which is the failure the literature reports.
- Gain: no GOAL change. It is the evidence base for any joint claim to the user.
- Falsifier: predicted pair-correlations within ±.05 of measured, and within-gate r > .3. If not, the predictions are only
  cluster-level.
- Cost: 0 GPU-h, CPU under 1 h, about half a day to build.

**B. Co-measured external cells as auxiliary multi-output supervision (HistoPlexer MP > SP; ISL transfer).**
- Mechanism: a shared trunk with a second stem for an external dataset where all markers are on every cell (e.g. S-BIAD452).
  Joint heads are trained only where co-measured; BSCCM single-stain heads are unchanged.
- Why it helps: the literature's joint gains come only from co-measured targets ("auxiliary morphological information from
  abundant markers"). This is the only route that adds genuine joint observations. It also adds positive events for CD19 and CD56
  (Infinity: rare-population markers have the lowest AUC).
- Expected gain: +.003 to .01 GOAL, if cross-modality transfer is about 25% efficient given K033 (+.015 to .02 per data doubling).
- Falsifier: 1 seed x 2 directions vs the existing control. Kill if under +.0054 overall and CD19/CD56 gain under .02.
  About 2 to 4 GPU-h, H100 (r50 at about .28 GPU-h per run plus the external epochs).
- Cost: 1 to 2 days for data plus the stem.

**C. Anchor/kNN imputation in the learned embedding (CyTOFmerge k = 50; Seurat-PCA won the 2025 benchmark).**
- Mechanism: on frozen trunk embeddings, predict each marker as the median over the 50 nearest training-draw cells of that
  marker's slides. Predict pooled profiles by copying from real 'all'-slide neighbours, which are jointly coherent by construction.
- Why it helps: a different inductive bias from the heads (non-parametric, no shrinkage to a regression mean). It also gives a
  real co-measured profile per cell for the pooled channels.
- Expected gain: +0 to .004 as a blend (the ensemble is saturated at +.002 per member).
- Falsifier: per-marker blend gain under .0027 (noise), reached at 0 GPU-h (CPU FAISS; about 0.1 GPU-h for embedding extraction).
- Cost: about 2 h.

**D. Infinity-style leave-one-marker-out transfer test (ISL "new label from minimal data").**
- Mechanism: drop one weak marker's slides from training, then fit a linear probe on 1 to 10% of its cells.
- Why it helps: it measures whether the trunk encodes a shared cell state that serves markers never co-measured. That is the
  premise of decoding profiles from single stains.
- Falsifier: probe r at 10% under 0.8 x the full-head r means the representation is marker-specific, so joint decoding rests on
  per-marker heads only.
- Cost: about 1 GPU-h (2 retrains), half a day.
# N077 data scout: public label-free leukocyte data that could help BSCCM LF->marker decoding

Date 2026-11-23. Read-only scout. Searched with WebSearch and WebFetch. Nothing was downloaded.
Quotes are verbatim from the page or tool extract. Anything not checked first-hand is marked [unverified].

## Bottom line
- Only one public set gives label-free images with **many markers per cell** on human whole-blood leukocytes: **S-BIAD452** (Lippeveld/Saeys, ImageStream). It is the top pick for joint decoding.
- No other LED-array/FPM leukocyte set with markers exists apart from BSCCM's own **BSCCM-coherent**.
- No large public label-free WBC set (>BSCCM) turned up for SSL. The large label-free blood sets are RT-DC flow brightfield, which is low-res and shows deformed cells (big gap).
- Reference ceiling: DeepIFC (60x IFC, 527k PBMC) still gets only CD19 r=.61 and CD56 r=.53, against CD45 .90. So weak markers stay weak even at 3x magnification. Our CD19 .32 has headroom, but ~.6 is a realistic external ceiling.

## Ranked list (usefulness for multi-marker LF->marker)

### 1. S-BIAD452 — human WBC imaging flow cytometry (Lippeveld, Saeys, Filby et al.)  [HIGH]
- URL: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/biostudies/BioImages/studies/S-BIAD452 ; files: https://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/biostudies/fire/S-BIAD/452/S-BIAD452/Files/human_wbc_ifc/
- Study text: "Four human whole blood samples were assayed on an ImageStream-X MK II imaging flow cytometer." "Two samples were stained for the identification of 8 white blood cell types."
- Single 9-colour tube, so **all markers are on every cell**: "CD15 FITC, Siglec-8 PE, CD14 PE-CF594, CD19 PerCP-Cy5.5, CD3 BV421, CD45 V500, CD4 BV605, CD56 APC, CD8 APC-Cy7" (API record). Channel names in filelist.json: BF1, BF2, SSC, CD15, Siglec8, CD14, CD19, CD3, CD45, CD4, CD56, CD8. There are also unstained/eosinophil-panel samples.
- Overlap with ours: CD45, CD3, CD19, CD56, CD14 (5/8). Missing: CD16, CD123, HLA-DR.
- Size: filelist.json lists 45 entries totalling 42,233,708,651 B (~42 GB): .cif 19.2 GB, zarr single-cell stores 17.1 GB, SCIP features.parquet 4.1 GB, plus .daf files with manual gating.
- Cells: the paper's labelled WBC set holds ~98k cells: "CD4+ T-cells 17,358; CD8+ 8,022; neutrophils 59,034; monocytes 2,655; B-cells 4,256; CD56+ NKT 2,214; other NKT 1,318; eosinophils 3,156" (bioRxiv 10.1101/680975 extract). B and NK cells are few.
- Modality: "using the 60x magnification", "0.25 μm per pixel". Two BF bands (420–480 nm, 570–595 nm) and SSC darkfield (laser side scatter).
- Licence: not stated on the record. BIA policy says "all new data directly submitted to the BioImage Archive will be made available under a CC0 or CC-BY-4.0 licence" (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/bioimage-archive/help-policies). Either works for academic use.
- How to use:
  - (a) Multi-task training with a second input stem: an IFC stem feeds a shared trunk and shared heads for the 5 overlapping markers. IFC cells carry joint labels, so they teach co-expression and exclusivity (CD3/CD19/CD56).
  - (b) A source of joint marker vectors for a structured or joint decoder prior.
  - (c) Extra SSL data.
- Modality gap: medium-high. Magnification is 3x ours. TDI-flow brightfield lacks the angular LED diversity. Laser SSC is not LED darkfield. The panel is per-sample compensated fluorescence intensity, not BSCCM's fluorescence.
- Cheapest test: pull one sample's zarr (a few GB) and resample BF1+SSC to the BSCCM pixel size. Then (i) run a frozen BSCCM encoder plus a ridge probe on CD19/CD56/CD3. (ii) Reverse direction: train the IFC multi-task model, then linear-probe its trunk on BSCCM CD19/HLA-DR against the in-domain SSL encoder. Under 1 GPU-h.

### 2. BSCCM-coherent (in-domain, same instrument)  [HIGH-MEDIUM, small]
- URL: https://waller-lab.github.io/BSCCM ; Dryad https://datadryad.org/dataset/doi:10.5061/dryad.sxksn038s ; paper https://arxiv.org/html/2402.06191v1
- Paper: "contains 566 different illumination patterns, each corresponding to illumination by a different single LED". "BSCCM-coherent contains only all-antibodies and no antibody conditions". "each dataset also contains fluorescence images in 6 channels".
- Size: 30 GB, 4,304 cells, 128x128 12-bit (tiny version: 100 cells, 0.6 GB). Licence: the arXiv page is CC BY 4.0; the dataset licence is not stated on the project page [unverified, Dryad default CC0].
- Use: there is no modality gap. Under incoherent illumination, any pattern is the sum of single-LED images. That allows:
  - learned-illumination search (Cooke/Horstmeyer, https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.04306: "optimized patterns result in up to a 45% performance improvement");
  - testing whether high-angle LEDs beyond our 24 channels carry CD19/HLA-DR signal;
  - FPM/QPI phase reconstruction as an extra input channel.
- Limits: only 4.3k cells and 'all' (pooled) labels only. Good for an evaluation or design study, too small to train a backbone.
- Cheapest test: synthesize our 24 channels from the single-LED stack, then compare a ridge/small-CNN pooled-channel r on 24 channels against all 566 LEDs (or PCA-64).

### 3. DeepIFC (Timonen et al., Cytometry A 2023)  [MEDIUM as reference/teacher, data NOT public]
- https://github.com/timonenv/DeepIFC ; https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2022.08.10.503433v2.full
- "The DeepIFC workflow and models trained on PBMC data are available under a permissible license." (repo: Apache-2.0). No data deposit found.
- Data: PBMC "n=527,107 cells", "Images were acquired at 60× magnification", BF Ch01/Ch09 + darkfield Ch12. Panel: CD45, CD14, CD19, CD8, CD3, CD56, 7-AAD.
- Per-marker r: CD45 .90, CD14 .88, CD3 .87, CD19 .61, CD56 .53, CD8 .41.
- Use: external ceiling and benchmark. The weights could serve as a frozen IFC teacher for S-BIAD452 pseudo-labels, though the U-Net was trained on a different instrument [unverified fit]. Ask the authors for the data.

### 4. BBBC045 (Nassar et al. 2019, ImageStream)  [MEDIUM-LOW]
- https://bbbc.broadinstitute.org/BBBC045 . Channels: "fluorescent, brightfield and darkfield". Classes: "B- and T-lymphocytes, eosinophils, monocytes and neutrophils". Labels: "The ground truth has been obtained by gating based on the appropriate corresponding fluorescent channels."
- 13 subjects, ~2.3 GB (591.6 MB populations, 1.58 GB montages, 170.6 MB CP features). CC0.
- Per-cell antibodies: FITC CD3/CD14/CD15/CD19 per search summary [unverified whether one marker per tube]. Gives class labels only.
- Use: a second IFC domain for the stem in #1, and a cheap transfer-evaluation set.

### 5. Cebinelli et al., BD FACSDiscover A8 + CellView, PB leukocytes (Mendeley)  [UNKNOWN, potentially MEDIUM]
- https://data.mendeley.com/datasets/rhjd7kg5by/2 (also 28sczzzddy, d432w939nf, s7vgdkx5dg, ky4svt2nyw). "acquired on a BD FACSDiscover™ A8 instrument equipped with BD CellView™ technology". CC BY 4.0.
- 10-marker panel per cell: CD5, CD4, CD8, CD14, CD15, CD19, CD45, CD56, PD-1, PD-L1. Overlap: CD45, CD14, CD19, CD56.
- The file lists rendered empty. Whether label-free image channels (light-loss/FSC/SSC images) are included is **[unverified]**; more likely FCS plus image-derived features.
- Cheapest test: open the Files tab by hand (5 min). If images are present, it is a second jointly labelled multi-marker source.

### 6. Guck lab deformability cytometry, blood cells + aggregates (OSF 3zkvw, 2026)  [LOW-MEDIUM; SSL/aux]
- https://osf.io/3zkvw ; paper https://arxiv.org/html/2609.07410 . "This dataset contains Deformability Cytometry data (.rtdc files) with images of blood cells and cell aggregates."
- Brightfield "250 × 80 pixel resolution, recorded at 3600 frames per second". Ground truth comes from antibody panels (lymphocytes CD19/CD3/CD56; neutrophils CD15/CD16/CD66; basophils CD123/CD203c; monocytes CD14).
- Files: train_data.zip 1.94 GB, test_data.zip 0.66 GB, WBCtest.zip 35 MB. About 15.6k WBCs train and 1.7k test. No licence set (node_license null).
- Gap: large (flow, deformed cells, low-res grayscale). Use as SSL or a class-auxiliary task only. Check whether the .rtdc files keep fl1-3 intensities (would give per-cell marker regression).

### 7. Immunological-synapse IFC (Dryad 10.5061/dryad.ht76hdrk7)  [LOW-MEDIUM, HLA-DR/CD3 only]
- https://datadryad.org/dataset/doi:10.5061/dryad.ht76hdrk7 . "over 2.8 million images"; "one bright field channel and multiple fluorescent channels". Markers: CD3, HLA-DR, phalloidin, pCD3ζ, viability. 124.94 GB in 4 zips. Licence: Dryad terms [unverified, Dryad is normally CC0].
- Cells: memory CD4 T cells plus an EBV B-LCL line, mostly conjugates. Activated or cell-line biology means a large biological gap. A possible weak HLA-DR auxiliary signal.

### 8. Smaller or partial sets  [LOW]
- **soRT-FDC** (DCOR, CC0): https://dcor.mpl.mpg.de/dataset/figshare-11302595-v1 . Blood RT-DC brightfield with "for identification of neutrophils (CD66+/CD14−)". DNN training files are included. Few markers.
- **IFC-seq human PBMC** (ImageStream, 82,109 cells, BF + CD3/CD8, 32x32 px): https://github.com/theislab/ifcseq . "all data used in this publication online at" (Google Drive). No licence.
- **LymphoMNIST**: https://arxiv.org/html/2503.12622v2 ; https://zenodo.org/records/17352233 (Apache-2.0). About 80k 64x64 **mouse** DIC images; "Splenocytes were FACS-sorted into T4, T8, and B subsets." Class only; species and modality gap.
- **Zenodo 5391155**: custom IFC of T cells (healthy vs Sézary), 2.2 GB, CC BY 4.0. T cells only, no markers stated.
- **ATOM time-stretch** (IEEE DataPort): https://ieee-dataport.org/documents/human-somatic-label-free-bright-field-cell-images . "asymmetric-detection time-stretch optical microscopy". Mostly cell lines with one PBMC class, 1.4 GB, subscription needed.

### 9. Marker co-expression priors without images (for joint decoding)  [MEDIUM idea, cheap]
- BSCCM is mostly single-stain, so the joint distribution of our 8 markers is weakly constrained. A public multi-colour flow panel gives an empirical joint prior. Uses:
  - a copula or flow prior on the joint head;
  - consistency checks against the 4 pooled 'all' channels;
  - synthetic joint targets.
- Candidate: OMIP-069, 40-colour PBMC, Cytek Aurora, FlowRepository FR-FCM-Z2QV ("40 color OMIP new donors unmixed"). Fluorofinder lists CD3, CD14, CD16, CD19, CD123. CD45, CD56 and HLA-DR are **[unverified]**. FlowRepository had a certificate error and a storage-limit notice.
- Gap: PBMC (no granulocytes) and a different intensity scale, so use rank/quantile-normalised values only.
- Cheapest test: fit a Gaussian copula on flow ranks, then check whether it predicts the observed correlation structure of BSCCM 'all'-slide pooled channels.

## Other LED-array / FPM / QPI data (checked, not useful for markers)
- FPM raw stacks exist only for tissue or targets: Siegen leech HDR-FPM on Zenodo (25.4 GB); an IEEE DataPort colour-FPM blood smear (files possibly absent); Glasgow lung/USAF (on request). There are no leukocyte+marker sets.
- QPI/ODT lymphocytes: Yoon 2017 (n=149/95/112, B/CD4/CD8, mouse) has no public data found. Deep-UV label-free hematology (Robles lab) has no data found. The HKU multi-ATOM T-cell data returned 403.
- arXiv 2605.14717 uses BSCCMNIST (DPC only, 28x28): "BSCCM provides paired DPC images, WBC labels, and quantitative protein-expression measurements". It reports composite-label r (CD16 .819, CD45 .799, CD3/CD19/CD56 .768, CD123/HLA-DR/CD14 .339). These are composite channels, **not comparable** to our per-marker numbers.
- Severin/Snijder PBMC "Phenoplex" (scDINO) is multiplexed immunofluorescence, not label-free, so it was excluded.

## Recommended order
1. S-BIAD452 one-sample pull: frozen-encoder ridge probe, then a 2-stem multi-task screen (1 seed) on the 5 overlapping markers. Watch BSCCM CD19/CD56 and joint metrics.
2. BSCCM-coherent: illumination/angle-content study for CD19/HLA-DR (CPU-feasible).
3. Flow-panel copula prior for the joint head (CPU only).
4. Check the Cebinelli Files tab by hand. If images are present, rank it next to #1.

#"'!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Donor-held-out S-BIAD452 joint decoding. See README.md for estimands and caveats."""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import copy
import hashlib
import json
import math
import os
from pathlib import Path
import random
import re
import signal
import time
from contextlib import nullcontext

import numpy as np
import torch
from torch import nn
from torch.nn import functional as F

MARKERS = ['"'CD15', 'Siglec8', 'CD14', 'CD19', 'CD3', 'CD45', 'CD4', 'CD56', 'CD8']
MI = {m: i for i, m in enumerate(MARKERS)}
POOL_MEMBERS = [MI[m] for m in ('CD3', 'CD19', 'CD56')]
VERSION = 1


def donor_ids(samples):
    out = []
    for sample in samples:
        match = re.fullmatch(r'sample([012])(?:_(?:early|late))?', str(sample))
        if match is None:
            raise ValueError(f'Unrecognised donor/sample: {sample"'!r}'"')
        out.append(int(match[1]))
    return np.asarray(out)


def donor_split(samples, test_donor):
    \"\"\"Fixed cyclic rule: test d, validation (d+1)%3, train (d+2)%3.\"\"\"
    d = donor_ids(samples)
    split = tuple(np.flatnonzero(d == k) for k in ((test_donor + 2) % 3,
                                                  (test_donor + 1) % 3, test_donor))
    if any(len(x) == 0 for x in split):
        raise ValueError('All three donors must be present (including in smoke packs).')
    return split


def reveal_masks(rows, regime, seed):
    \"\"\"Stateless per packed-row seed; masks do not change with epoch, subset, or resume.\"\"\"
    rows = np.asarray(rows, dtype=np.uint64)
    # SplitMix64: independent streams for marker and panel assignment.
    def uniform(stream):
        with np.errstate(over='ignore'):
            z = rows + np.uint64(seed) + np.uint64(stream)
            z = (z "'^ (z >> np.uint64(30))) * np.uint64(0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9)
            z = (z ''^ (z >> np.uint64(27))) * np.uint64(0x94d049bb133111eb)
            z ''^= z >> np.uint64(31)
        return (z >> np.uint64(11)).astype(np.float64) / 2**53
    mask = np.zeros((len(rows), 9), bool)
    pool = np.zeros((len(rows), 2), bool)
    if regime == '"'full':
        mask[:] = True
    elif regime in ('single', 'single_pooled'):
        mask[np.arange(len(rows)), np.minimum((uniform(0x12345) * 9).astype(int), 8)] = True
        if regime == 'single_pooled':
            pooled = uniform(0x98765) < 0.1
            mask[pooled] = False
            pool[pooled] = True
    else:
        raise ValueError(regime)
    return mask, pool


def masked_mse(pred, target, mask):
    # Select BEFORE subtraction: NaNs or arbitrary hidden labels cannot enter loss.
    if not mask.any():
        return pred.sum() * 0
    return (pred[mask] - target[mask]).square().mean()


def robust_scale(x):
    return max(float(1.4826 * np.median(np.abs(x - np.median(x)))), 1.0)


def fit_pool_calibration(raw, y, single_mask, pooled_mask):
    \"\"\"Fit only revealed singles/pooled observations, never hidden component values.\"\"\"
    visible = pooled_mask[:, 0]
    if visible.sum() < 2:
        raise ValueError('single_pooled needs >=2 pooled TRAIN cells; increase smoke --max-train.')
    sums = raw[:, POOL_MEMBERS].sum(1)
    c = robust_scale(sums[visible])
    # P1 = asinh(linear intensity sum / c); P2 = linear CD45, as requested.
    p = np.stack([np.arcsinh(sums / c), raw[:, MI['CD45']]], 1)
    mean, std = p[visible].mean(0), np.maximum(p[visible].std(0), 1e-6)
    slope, bias = np.ones(9), np.zeros(9)
    for j in range(9):
        obs = single_mask[:, j]
        if obs.sum() < 2:
            raise ValueError(f'No inverse-map calibration support for {MARKERS[j]}; increase training rows.')
        x, t = y[obs, j], np.arcsinh(raw[obs, j] / c)
        a = np.mean((x - x.mean()) * (t - t.mean())) / max(float(x.var()), 1e-8)
        slope[j] = np.clip(a, 1e-3, 20)
        bias[j] = np.clip(t.mean() - slope[j] * x.mean(), -15, 15)
    return dict(c=c, mean=mean.tolist(), std=std.tolist(), slope=slope.tolist(), bias=bias.tolist(),
                n_pooled=int(visible.sum()), n_single=single_mask.sum(0).tolist())


def pooled_targets(raw, calibration):
    p = np.stack([np.arcsinh(raw[:, POOL_MEMBERS].sum(1) / calibration['c']),
                  raw[:, MI['CD45']]], 1)
    return ((p - calibration['mean']) / calibration['std']).astype(np.float32)


class MonotoneInverse(nn.Module):
    \"\"\"y -> c*sinh(positive_slope*y+bias), jointly learned using revealed data only.\"\"\"
    def __init__(self, calibration):
        super().__init__()
        slopes = torch.tensor(calibration['slope'], dtype=torch.float32)
        self.log_slope = nn.Parameter(torch.log(torch.expm1(slopes)))
        self.bias = nn.Parameter(torch.tensor(calibration['bias'], dtype=torch.float32))
        self.register_buffer('c', torch.tensor(calibration['c'], dtype=torch.float32))
        self.register_buffer('mean', torch.tensor(calibration['mean'], dtype=torch.float32))
        self.register_buffer('std', torch.tensor(calibration['std'], dtype=torch.float32))

    def transformed(self, y):
        return F.softplus(self.log_slope) * y + self.bias

    def forward(self, y):
        # Saturation protects sinh under runaway predictions; map remains nondecreasing.
        raw_over_c = torch.sinh(self.transformed(y.float()).clamp(-20, 20))
        p = torch.stack([torch.asinh(raw_over_c[:, POOL_MEMBERS].sum(1)),
                         self.c * raw_over_c[:, MI['CD45']]], 1)
        return (p - self.mean) / self.std


class SandboxModel(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, cov_rank=0, pooled_mode='none', calibration=None, tiny=False):
        super().__init__()
        if tiny:
            self.encoder = nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(3, 8, 3, stride=4, padding=1), nn.ReLU(),
                                         nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1), nn.Flatten())
            nf = 8
        else:
            import timm
            self.encoder = timm.create_model('resnet50', pretrained=False, in_chans=3, num_classes=0)
            nf = self.encoder.num_features
        self.mean = nn.Linear(nf, 9)
        self.rank = cov_rank
        self.cov = nn.Linear(nf, 9 * (1 + cov_rank)) if cov_rank else None
        self.pool_head = nn.Linear(nf, 2) if pooled_mode == 'head' else None
        self.inverse = MonotoneInverse(calibration) if pooled_mode == 'inverse' else None

    def forward(self, x):
        f = self.encoder(x)
        mu = self.mean(f)
        cov = None
        if self.cov is not None:
            z = self.cov(f).float()
            cov = (F.softplus(z[:, :9]) + 1e-4, z[:, 9:].reshape(-1, 9, self.rank))
        pool = self.pool_head(f) if self.pool_head is not None else None
        if self.inverse is not None:
            pool = self.inverse(mu)
        return mu, pool, cov, f


def gaussian_nll(mu, y, cov, reduction='mean'):
    diag, factor = cov
    covariance = torch.diag_embed(diag.float()) + factor.float() @ factor.float().transpose(-1, -2)
    chol = torch.linalg.cholesky(covariance)
    error = (y.float() - mu.float()).unsqueeze(-1)
    mahal = (error * torch.cholesky_solve(error, chol)).sum((-1, -2))
    nll = 0.5 * (mahal + 2 * chol.diagonal(dim1=-2, dim2=-1).log().sum(-1) + 9 * math.log(2 * math.pi))
    return nll.mean() if reduction == 'mean' else nll


class Cells(torch.utils.data.Dataset):
    def __init__(self, pack, rows):
        self.path, self.rows = str(Path(pack) / 'lf.npy'), np.asarray(rows)
        self.images = None

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.rows)

    def __getitem__(self, index):
        if self.images is None:
            self.images = np.load(self.path, mmap_mode='r')
        row = int(self.rows[index])
        return torch.from_numpy(np.array(self.images[row], dtype=np.float32)), row


def augment(x):
    \"\"\"Independent D4 rotations/reflections and zero-filled +-4px shifts per cell.\"\"\"
    n, _, h, w = x.shape
    k = torch.randint(4, (n,), device=x.device)
    out = torch.empty_like(x)
    for rotation in range(4):
        select = k == rotation
        out[select] = torch.rot90(x[select], rotation, (-2, -1))
    flip = torch.rand(n, device=x.device) < 0.5
    out[flip] = out[flip].flip(-1)
    shifts = torch.randint(-4, 5, (n, 2), device=x.device)
    yy = torch.arange(h, device=x.device)[None, :, None] - shifts[:, 0, None, None]
    xx = torch.arange(w, device=x.device)[None, None, :] - shifts[:, 1, None, None]
    valid = (yy >= 0) & (yy < h) & (xx >= 0) & (xx < w)
    shifted = out.permute(0, 2, 3, 1)[torch.arange(n, device=x.device)[:, None, None],
                                        yy.clamp(0, h - 1), xx.clamp(0, w - 1)]
    return (shifted * valid[..., None]).permute(0, 3, 1, 2).contiguous()


def pearson(a, b):
    a, b = np.asarray(a, dtype=np.float64), np.asarray(b, dtype=np.float64)
    if len(a) < 3:
        return None
    a, b = a - a.mean(), b - b.mean()
    denom = np.linalg.norm(a) * np.linalg.norm(b)
    return float(np.clip(a @ b / denom, -1, 1)) if denom > 1e-12 else None


def average_defined(values):
    good = [v for v in values if v is not None]
    return float(np.mean(good)) if good else None


def marker_correlations(y):
    return [[pearson(y[:, i], y[:, j]) for j in range(9)] for i in range(9)]


def fit_gates(train_y):
    \"\"\"Evaluation-only empirical thresholds, never supplied to model/loss.\"\"\"
    return dict(positive=np.quantile(train_y, .75, axis=0).tolist(),
                cd45_hi=float(np.quantile(train_y[:, MI['CD45']], .25)),
                cd15_lo=float(np.quantile(train_y[:, MI['CD15']], .5)))


def gate_masks(y, gates):
    pos = y > np.asarray(gates['positive'])
    cd = lambda m: pos[:, MI[m]]
    wbc = y[:, MI['CD45']] > gates['cd45_hi']
    lymph = wbc & (y[:, MI['CD15']] <= gates['cd15_lo']) & ~cd('CD14')
    gran = wbc & cd('CD15')
    mono = wbc & ~cd('CD15') & cd('CD14')
    return dict(lymphocytes=lymph, granulocytes=gran, monocytes=mono,
                T_cells=lymph & cd('CD3'), B_cells=lymph & ~cd('CD3') & cd('CD19'),
                NK_cells=lymph & ~cd('CD3') & ~cd('CD19') & cd('CD56'),
                CD4_T=lymph & cd('CD3') & cd('CD4'), CD8_T=lymph & cd('CD3') & cd('CD8'),
                eosinophils=gran & cd('Siglec8'), CD3_CD19_DP=cd('CD3') & cd('CD19'))


def coarse_populations(y, gates):
    masks = gate_masks(y, gates)
    assigned = np.zeros(len(y), bool)
    out = {}
    for name in ('lymphocytes', 'granulocytes', 'monocytes'):
        out[name] = masks[name]
        assigned |= out[name]
    out['other'] = ~assigned
    return out


def correlation_fidelity(y, p):
    t, q = marker_correlations(y), marker_correlations(p)
    valid = [(i, j) for i in range(9) for j in range(9)
             if t[i][j] is not None and q[i][j] is not None]
    # Undefined correlations are not replaced with zero or silently scored as correct.
    frob = math.sqrt(sum((q[i][j] - t[i][j]) ** 2 for i, j in valid)) if valid else None
    return dict(n=int(len(y)), frobenius=frob, valid_entries=len(valid), total_entries=81,
                true=t, predicted=q)


def fscore(truth, prediction):
    tp = int((truth & prediction).sum())
    fp = int((~truth & prediction).sum())
    fn = int((truth & ~prediction).sum())
    denom = 2 * tp + fp + fn
    return dict(f1=2 * tp / denom if denom else None, tp=tp, fp=fp, fn=fn,
                true_count=int(truth.sum()), predicted_count=int(prediction.sum()))


def compute_metrics(y, p, gates):
    y, p = np.asarray(y, np.float64), np.asarray(p, np.float64)
    if y.shape "'!= p.shape or y.ndim != 2 or y.shape[1] != 9 or not np.isfinite([y, p]).all():
        raise ValueError('"'Metrics require finite matching (N,9) truth and predictions.')
    r = {m: pearson(y[:, j], p[:, j]) for j, m in enumerate(MARKERS)}
    rmse = np.sqrt(np.mean((y - p) ** 2, axis=1))
    norms = np.linalg.norm(y, axis=1) * np.linalg.norm(p, axis=1)
    cos = np.divide((y * p).sum(1), norms, out=np.full(len(y), np.nan), where=norms > 1e-12)
    populations = coarse_populations(y, gates)
    coexpression = {'overall': correlation_fidelity(y, p)}
    within = {}
    means_y, means_p = [], []
    for name, mask in populations.items():
        coexpression[name] = correlation_fidelity(y[mask], p[mask])
        rr = {m: pearson(y[mask, j], p[mask, j]) for j, m in enumerate(MARKERS)}
        within[name] = dict(n=int(mask.sum()), per_marker_r=rr, macro_r=average_defined(rr.values()))
        if mask.any():
            means_y.append(y[mask].mean(0))
            means_p.append(p[mask].mean(0))
    cluster_r = {m: pearson(np.asarray(means_y)[:, j], np.asarray(means_p)[:, j])
                 for j, m in enumerate(MARKERS)}
    pair_delta = {}
    for i in range(9):
        for j in range(i + 1, 9):
            tr, pr = pearson(y[:, i], y[:, j]), pearson(p[:, i], p[:, j])
            pair_delta[f'{MARKERS[i]}--{MARKERS[j]}'] = dict(true_r=tr, predicted_r=pr,
                predicted_minus_true=None if tr is None or pr is None else pr - tr)
    key_pairs = {}
    for pop in ('lymphocytes', 'granulocytes'):
        mask = populations[pop]
        key_pairs[pop] = {}
        for a, b in [('CD3', 'CD19'), ('CD3', 'CD56'), ('CD4', 'CD8'), ('CD14', 'CD15')]:
            key_pairs[pop][f'{a}--{b}'] = dict(n=int(mask.sum()),
                true_r=pearson(y[mask, MI[a]], y[mask, MI[b]]),
                predicted_r=pearson(p[mask, MI[a]], p[mask, MI[b]]))
    true_gates, pred_gates = gate_masks(y, gates), gate_masks(p, gates)
    gating = {name: fscore(mask, pred_gates[name]) for name, mask in true_gates.items()}
    return dict(per_marker_r=r, macro_r=average_defined(r.values()),
                vector_rmse_mean=float(rmse.mean()), vector_rmse_median=float(np.median(rmse)),
                vector_cosine_mean=float(np.nanmean(cos)) if np.isfinite(cos).any() else None,
                vector_cosine_defined=int(np.isfinite(cos).sum()),
                coexpression=coexpression, within_population=within,
                population_means=dict(n_populations=len(means_y), per_marker_r=cluster_r,
                                      macro_r=average_defined(cluster_r.values())),
                pairwise_correlation_bias=pair_delta, key_pairs=key_pairs, gating=gating,
                double_positive_CD3_CD19=dict(true_rate=float(true_gates['CD3_CD19_DP'].mean()),
                                              predicted_rate=float(pred_gates['CD3_CD19_DP'].mean())))


def knn_impute(train_features, test_features, train_y, mask, k=50, query_chunk=256, reference_chunk=4096):
    \"\"\"Exact Euclidean KNN; both axes chunked. Every marker has its own revealed bank.\"\"\"
    if k < 1:
        raise ValueError('K must be positive.')
    train_features = torch.as_tensor(train_features, dtype=torch.float32)
    test_features = torch.as_tensor(test_features, dtype=torch.float32)
    result = np.empty((len(test_features), 9), np.float32)
    counts = []
    for j in range(9):
        selected = np.flatnonzero(mask[:, j])
        if not len(selected):
            raise ValueError(f'No revealed training neighbours for {MARKERS[j]}')
        kk = min(k, len(selected))
        counts.append(dict(marker=MARKERS[j], bank_size=len(selected), effective_k=kk))
        bank, values = train_features[selected], np.asarray(train_y)[selected, j]
        for start in range(0, len(test_features), query_chunk):
            q = test_features[start:start + query_chunk]
            distances = torch.full((len(q), kk), float('inf'))
            indices = torch.zeros((len(q), kk), dtype=torch.long)
            for ref in range(0, len(bank), reference_chunk):
                b = bank[ref:ref + reference_chunk]
                dist = (q.square().sum(1)[:, None] + b.square().sum(1)[None] - 2 * q @ b.T).clamp_min_(0)
                ids = torch.arange(ref, ref + len(b))[None].expand(len(q), -1)
                combined = torch.cat([distances, dist], 1)
                distances, pos = combined.topk(kk, dim=1, largest=False, sorted=True)
                indices = torch.cat([indices, ids], 1).gather(1, pos)
            result[start:start + len(q), j] = values[indices.numpy()].mean(1)
    return result, counts


def write_json(path, value):
    temp = Path(str(path) + '.tmp')
    with temp.open('w') as handle:
        json.dump(value, handle, indent=2, allow_nan=False)
    os.replace(temp, path)


def save_checkpoint(path, payload):
    temp = str(path) + '.tmp'
    torch.save(payload, temp)
    os.replace(temp, path)


def rng_state():
    return dict(python=random.getstate(), numpy=np.random.get_state(), torch=torch.get_rng_state(),
                cuda=torch.cuda.get_rng_state_all() if torch.cuda.is_available() else [])


def restore_rng(state):
    random.setstate(state['python'])
    np.random.set_state(state['numpy'])
    torch.set_rng_state(state['torch'].cpu())
    if state['cuda']:
        torch.cuda.set_rng_state_all([x.cpu() for x in state['cuda']])


def epoch_batches(rows, batch_size, seed, epoch):
    order = np.random.default_rng(np.random.SeedSequence([seed, epoch])).permutation(rows)
    batches = [order[i:i + batch_size] for i in range(0, len(order), batch_size)]
    # BatchNorm cannot train on a singleton. Keep that cell by merging the last batch.
    if len(batches) > 1 and len(batches[-1]) == 1:
        batches[-2] = np.concatenate([batches[-2], batches[-1]])
        batches.pop()
    return batches


def loader(pack, rows, args, batches=None):
    # Separate generator: constructing/skipping loaders must not consume augmentation RNG.
    generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(args.seed + 101)
    kw = dict(num_workers=args.workers, pin_memory=args.device == 'cuda', generator=generator)
    if batches is None:
        return torch.utils.data.DataLoader(Cells(pack, rows), batch_size=args.bs, **kw)
    # Cells rows are flattened, and batch_sampler indexes that same flattened sequence.
    sizes = [len(b) for b in batches]
    offsets = np.cumsum([0] + sizes)
    sampler = [list(range(offsets[i], offsets[i + 1])) for i in range(len(sizes))]
    return torch.utils.data.DataLoader(Cells(pack, np.concatenate(batches)), batch_sampler=sampler, **kw)


def autocast(args):
    return torch.autocast('cuda', dtype=torch.bfloat16) if args.device == 'cuda' else nullcontext()


def batch_loss(model, output, ids, targets, masks, pools, pool_masks, raw, calibration, args):
    mu, pp, cov, _ = output
    y = targets[ids].to(args.device)
    mask = masks[ids].to(args.device)
    loss = gaussian_nll(mu, y, cov) if cov is not None else masked_mse(mu.float(), y, mask)
    if pp is not None:
        loss = loss + args.pool_weight * masked_mse(pp.float(), pools[ids].to(args.device),
                                                   pool_masks[ids].to(args.device))
    if model.inverse is not None and args.map_weight:
        # These are the SAME observed single stains, in raw/c coordinates; no extra labels.
        observed_raw = raw[ids].to(args.device)
        map_target = torch.asinh(observed_raw / calibration['c'])
        loss = loss + args.map_weight * masked_mse(model.inverse.transformed(y), map_target, mask)
    return loss


@torch.no_grad()
def validation_loss(model, pack, rows, scale, tensors, calibration, args):
    model.eval()
    total, count = 0., 0
    for x, ids in loader(pack, rows, args):
        with autocast(args):
            output = model(x.to(args.device) / scale)
            loss = batch_loss(model, output, ids, *tensors, calibration, args)
        # Skip cells without any observations (there are none for the supported regimes).
        total += float(loss) * len(x)
        count += len(x)
    return total / count


@torch.no_grad()
def predict(model, pack, rows, scale, args):
    model.eval()
    means, features, diagonals, factors = [], [], [], []
    for x, _ in loader(pack, rows, args):
        with autocast(args):
            mu, _, cov, embedding = model(x.to(args.device) / scale)
        means.append(mu.float().cpu().numpy())
        features.append(embedding.float().cpu().numpy())
        if cov is not None:
            diagonals.append(cov[0].cpu().numpy())
            factors.append(cov[1].cpu().numpy())
    return (np.concatenate(means), np.concatenate(features),
            (np.concatenate(diagonals), np.concatenate(factors)) if diagonals else None)


def parse_args(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    ap.add_argument('--pack', default='/hnvme/workspace/v181bb10-bsccm/external/sbiad452_pack')
    ap.add_argument('--out', required=True)
    ap.add_argument('--regime', choices=['full', 'single', 'single_pooled'], default='single')
    ap.add_argument('--test-donor', type=int, choices=[0, 1, 2], required=True)
    ap.add_argument('--pooled-mode', choices=['inverse', 'head'], default='inverse')
    ap.add_argument('--cov-rank', type=int, choices=[0, 2], default=0)
    ap.add_argument('--epochs', type=int, default=15)
    ap.add_argument('--bs', type=int, default=256)
    ap.add_argument('--lr', type=float, default=5e-4)
    ap.add_argument('--pool-weight', type=float, default=1.)
    ap.add_argument('--map-weight', type=float, default=.1)
    ap.add_argument('--knn-impute', type=int, default=50, metavar='K', help='0 disables the baseline')
    ap.add_argument('--knn-query-chunk', type=int, default=256)
    ap.add_argument('--knn-reference-chunk', type=int, default=4096)
    ap.add_argument('--seed', type=int, default=42)
    ap.add_argument('--workers', type=int, default=4)
    ap.add_argument('--device', choices=['cpu', 'cuda'], default='cuda')
    ap.add_argument('--threads', type=int, default=4)
    ap.add_argument('--checkpoint-every', type=int, default=200)
    ap.add_argument('--max-train', type=int, default=0)
    ap.add_argument('--max-val', type=int, default=0)
    ap.add_argument('--max-test', type=int, default=0)
    ap.add_argument('--smoke-tiny-model', action='store_true', help='testing ONLY; replaces resnet50')
    ap.add_argument('--stop-after-steps', type=int, default=0, help='testing: interrupt after N new steps')
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
    if a.cov_rank and a.regime "'!= '"'full':
        ap.error('--cov-rank 2 requires --regime full')
    for name in ('epochs', 'threads', 'checkpoint_every', 'knn_query_chunk', 'knn_reference_chunk'):
        if getattr(a, name) < 1:
            ap.error(f'{name} must be positive')
    if a.bs < 2:
        ap.error('--bs must be >=2')
    for name in ('seed', 'workers', 'knn_impute', 'max_train', 'max_val', 'max_test', 'stop_after_steps'):
        if getattr(a, name) < 0:
            ap.error(f'{name} must be nonnegative')
    if not np.isfinite(a.lr) or a.lr <= 0:
        ap.error('--lr must be finite and positive')
    for name in ('pool_weight', 'map_weight'):
        if not np.isfinite(getattr(a, name)) or getattr(a, name) < 0:
            ap.error(f'{name} must be finite and nonnegative')
    return a


def main(argv=None):
    args = parse_args(argv)
    torch.set_num_threads(args.threads)
    random.seed(args.seed)
    np.random.seed(args.seed)
    torch.manual_seed(args.seed)
    if args.device == 'cuda' and not torch.cuda.is_available():
        raise SystemExit('CUDA unavailable: use --device cpu for tiny smoke tests.')
    pack, out = Path(args.pack).resolve(), Path(args.out).resolve()
    if out == pack or pack in out.parents:
        raise ValueError('--out must not be inside the read-only pack.')
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with np.load(pack / 'labels.npz', allow_pickle=False) as data:
        labels = {k: data[k] for k in data.files}
    y, raw = labels['Y'].astype(np.float32), labels['I_raw'].astype(np.float32)
    if list(labels['names'].astype(str)) "'!= MARKERS or y.shape != raw.shape or y.shape[1:] != (9,):
        raise ValueError('"'Expected canonical nine-marker schema.')
    if not np.isfinite(y).all() or not np.isfinite(raw).all():
        raise ValueError('All packed cells must have nine finite measurements.')
    images = np.load(pack / 'lf.npy', mmap_mode='r')
    if images.shape "'!= (len(y), 3, 128, 128) or images.dtype != np.float16:
        raise ValueError('"'Expected float16 lf.npy (N,3,128,128).')
    chan_scale = np.asarray(labels['chan_scale'], dtype=np.float32)
    if chan_scale.shape "'!= (3,) or not np.isfinite(chan_scale).all() or (chan_scale <= 0).any():
        raise ValueError('"'chan_scale must contain three positive finite values.')
    scale = torch.tensor(chan_scale, device=args.device)[None, :, None, None]
    tr, va, te = donor_split(labels['sample'], args.test_donor)
    for rows, limit in ((tr, args.max_train), (va, args.max_val), (te, args.max_test)):
        pass
    def subset(rows, limit, stream):
        return np.sort(np.random.default_rng(args.seed + stream).choice(rows, min(limit, len(rows)), replace=False)) if limit else rows
    tr, va, te = subset(tr, args.max_train, 1), subset(va, args.max_val, 2), subset(te, args.max_test, 3)
    if len(tr) < 2:
        raise ValueError('Need >=2 training cells.')
    masks, pool_masks = reveal_masks(np.arange(len(y)), args.regime, args.seed)
    calibration = fit_pool_calibration(raw[tr], y[tr], masks[tr], pool_masks[tr]) if args.regime == 'single_pooled' else None
    pools = pooled_targets(raw, calibration) if calibration else np.zeros((len(y), 2), np.float32)
    # Seal supervision: hidden training labels are replaced by zero before constructing tensors.
    visible_y = np.where(masks, y, 0).astype(np.float32)
    visible_raw = np.where(masks, raw, 0).astype(np.float32)
    pools = np.where(pool_masks, pools, 0).astype(np.float32)
    tensors = tuple(torch.from_numpy(x) for x in (visible_y, masks, pools, pool_masks, visible_raw))
    mode = args.pooled_mode if args.regime == 'single_pooled' else 'none'
    model = SandboxModel(args.cov_rank, mode, calibration, args.smoke_tiny_model).to(args.device)
    opt = torch.optim.AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=args.lr, weight_decay=.05)
    steps_per_epoch = len(epoch_batches(tr, args.bs, args.seed, 0))
    total_steps = args.epochs * steps_per_epoch
    scheduler = torch.optim.lr_scheduler.OneCycleLR(opt, args.lr, total_steps=total_steps, pct_start=.1)
    excluded = {'out', 'workers', 'threads', 'checkpoint_every', 'stop_after_steps',
                'knn_impute', 'knn_query_chunk', 'knn_reference_chunk'}
    cfg = {k: v for k, v in vars(args).items() if k not in excluded}
    cfg['pack'] = str(pack)
    cfg['version'] = VERSION
    cfg['labels_sha256'] = hashlib.sha256((pack / 'labels.npz').read_bytes()).hexdigest()
    stat = (pack / 'lf.npy').stat()
    cfg['lf_stat'] = [stat.st_size, stat.st_mtime_ns]
    ckpt_path = out / 'ckpt.pt'
    epoch, batch, step, loss_sum, loss_count = 0, 0, 0, 0., 0
    best_loss, best_state, history = math.inf, None, []
    resumed = False
    if ckpt_path.exists():
        ckpt = torch.load(ckpt_path, map_location='cpu', weights_only=False)
        if ckpt['cfg'] "'!= cfg or any(not np.array_equal(ckpt[k], v) for k, v in [('"'tr', tr), ('va', va), ('te', te)]):
            raise ValueError('Refusing resume: recipe, pack fingerprint, or donor rows changed.')
        model.load_state_dict(ckpt['model'])
        opt.load_state_dict(ckpt['optimizer'])
        scheduler.load_state_dict(ckpt['scheduler'])
        epoch, batch, step = ckpt['epoch'], ckpt['batch'], ckpt['step']
        loss_sum, loss_count = ckpt['loss_sum'], ckpt['loss_count']
        best_loss, best_state, history = ckpt['best_loss'], ckpt['best_state'], ckpt['history']
        restore_rng(ckpt['rng'])
        resumed = True
        print(f'Resumed epoch={epoch} batch={batch} step={step}', flush=True)
    setup = dict(cfg=cfg, split=dict(train_donor=(args.test_donor + 2) % 3,
                                   validation_donor=(args.test_donor + 1) % 3, test_donor=args.test_donor,
                                   n_train=len(tr), n_validation=len(va), n_test=len(te)),
                 n_revealed_singles=masks[tr].sum(0).tolist(), n_pooled_cells=int(pool_masks[tr, 0].sum()),
                 pool_calibration=calibration, architecture='tiny_smoke' if args.smoke_tiny_model else 'resnet50',
                 target_normalization='Pack Y: per-sample z scores using all sample cells (retrospective calibration).',
                 pooled_normalization='Fit training donor revealed pooled cells; freeze for validation/test.')
    write_json(out / 'setup.json', setup)
    stop = {'signal': None}
    def request_stop(signum, frame):
        stop['signal'] = signal.Signals(signum).name
    old_handlers = {s: signal.signal(s, request_stop) for s in (signal.SIGUSR1, signal.SIGTERM)}
    start_step, start_time = step, time.monotonic()
    def checkpoint():
        save_checkpoint(ckpt_path, dict(cfg=cfg, model=model.state_dict(), optimizer=opt.state_dict(),
            scheduler=scheduler.state_dict(), epoch=epoch, batch=batch, step=step,
            loss_sum=loss_sum, loss_count=loss_count, best_loss=best_loss, best_state=best_state,
            history=history, tr=tr, va=va, te=te, rng=rng_state()))
    try:
        while epoch < args.epochs:
            batches = epoch_batches(tr, args.bs, args.seed, epoch)
            model.train()
            if batch < len(batches):
                for x, ids in loader(pack, tr, args, batches[batch:]):
                    opt.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
                    with autocast(args):
                        output = model(augment(x.to(args.device) / scale))
                        loss = batch_loss(model, output, ids, *tensors, calibration, args)
                    if not torch.isfinite(loss):
                        raise FloatingPointError('Nonfinite loss; last good checkpoint is preserved.')
                    loss.backward()
                    torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), 10.)
                    opt.step()
                    scheduler.step()
                    step += 1
                    batch += 1
                    loss_sum += float(loss.detach()) * len(x)
                    loss_count += len(x)
                    if args.stop_after_steps and step - start_step >= args.stop_after_steps:
                        stop['signal'] = 'test_stop_after_steps'
                    if step % args.checkpoint_every == 0 or stop['signal']:
                        checkpoint()
                    if stop['signal']:
                        write_json(out / 'result.json', dict(status='interrupted', reason=stop['signal'],
                                   epoch=epoch, batch=batch, step=step, resumed=resumed))
                        return 0
            val = validation_loss(model, pack, va, scale, tensors, calibration, args)
            if not np.isfinite(val):
                raise FloatingPointError('Nonfinite validation loss.')
            if val < best_loss:
                best_loss = val
                best_state = {k: v.detach().cpu().clone() for k, v in model.state_dict().items()}
            history.append(dict(epoch=epoch + 1, step=step, train_loss=loss_sum / loss_count, validation_loss=val))
            print(json.dumps(history[-1]), flush=True)
            epoch, batch, loss_sum, loss_count = epoch + 1, 0, 0., 0
            checkpoint()
            if stop['signal']:
                write_json(out / 'result.json', dict(status='interrupted', reason=stop['signal'], epoch=epoch, step=step))
                return 0
        # Only the fixed validation donor selects the checkpoint. Test donor is scored once here.
        model.load_state_dict(best_state)
        prediction, test_features, cov = predict(model, pack, te, scale, args)
        gates = fit_gates(y[tr])  # evaluation only; full train truth never feeds any loss or representation
        metrics = compute_metrics(y[te], prediction, gates)
        payload = dict(P=prediction, Y=y[te], rows=te, names=np.asarray(MARKERS), sample=labels['sample'][te],
                       vector_rmse=np.sqrt(np.mean((prediction - y[te]) ** 2, axis=1)))
        for key in ('part', 'object_number'):
            if key in labels:
                payload[key] = labels[key][te]
        if cov is not None:
            payload.update(cov_diag=cov[0], cov_factor=cov[1])
            metrics['gaussian_nll'] = float(gaussian_nll(torch.from_numpy(prediction), torch.from_numpy(y[te]),
                                          tuple(torch.from_numpy(a) for a in cov)))
        if args.knn_impute:

class MonotoneInverse(nn.Module):
    \"\"\"y -> c*sinh(positive_slope*y+bias), jointly learned using revealed data only.\"\"\"
    def __init__(self, calibration):
        super().__init__()
        slopes = torch.tensor(calibration['slope'], dtype=torch.float32)
        self.log_slope = nn.Parameter(torch.log(torch.expm1(slopes)))
        self.bias = nn.Parameter(torch.tensor(calibration['bias'], dtype=torch.float32))
        self.register_buffer('c', torch.tensor(calibration['c'], dtype=torch.float32))
        self.register_buffer('mean', torch.tensor(calibration['mean'], dtype=torch.float32))
        self.register_buffer('std', torch.tensor(calibration['std'], dtype=torch.float32))

    def transformed(self, y):
        return F.softplus(self.log_slope) * y + self.bias

    def forward(self, y):

        raw_over_c = torch.sinh(self.transformed(y.float()).clamp(-20, 20))
        p = torch.stack([torch.asinh(raw_over_c[:, POOL_MEMBERS].sum(1)),
                         self.c * raw_over_c[:, MI['CD45']]], 1)
        return (p - self.mean) / self.std

    def __init__(self, cov_rank=0, pooled_mode='none', calibration=None, tiny=False):

def gaussian_nll(mu, y, cov, reduction='mean'):
    diag, factor = cov
    covariance = torch.diag_embed(diag.float()) + factor.float() @ factor.float().transpose(-1, -2)
    chol = torch.linalg.cholesky(covariance)
    error = (y.float() - mu.float()).unsqueeze(-1)
    mahal = (error * torch.cholesky_solve(error, chol)).sum((-1, -2))
    nll = 0.5 * (mahal + 2 * chol.diagonal(dim1=-2, dim2=-1).log().sum(-1) + 9 * math.log(2 * math.pi))
    return nll.mean() if reduction == 'mean' else nll

def augment(x):
    \"\"\"Independent D4 rotations/reflections and zero-filled +-4px shifts per cell.\"\"\"
    n, _, h, w = x.shape
    k = torch.randint(4, (n,), device=x.device)
    out = torch.empty_like(x)
    for rotation in range(4):
        select = k == rotation
        out[select] = torch.rot90(x[select], rotation, (-2, -1))
    flip = torch.rand(n, device=x.device) < 0.5
    out[flip] = out[flip].flip(-1)
    shifts = torch.randint(-4, 5, (n, 2), device=x.device)
    yy = torch.arange(h, device=x.device)[None, :, None] - shifts[:, 0, None, None]
    xx = torch.arange(w, device=x.device)[None, None, :] - shifts[:, 1, None, None]
    valid = (yy >= 0) & (yy < h) & (xx >= 0) & (xx < w)
    shifted = out.permute(0, 2, 3, 1)[torch.arange(n, device=x.device)[:, None, None],
                                        yy.clamp(0, h - 1), xx.clamp(0, w - 1)]
    return (shifted * valid[..., None]).permute(0, 3, 1, 2).contiguous()


def pearson(a, b):
    a, b = np.asarray(a, dtype=np.float64), np.asarray(b, dtype=np.float64)
    if len(a) < 3:
        return None
    a, b = a - a.mean(), b - b.mean()
    denom = np.linalg.norm(a) * np.linalg.norm(b)
    return float(np.clip(a @ b / denom, -1, 1)) if denom > 1e-12 else None

    good = [v for v in values if v is not None]
    return float(np.mean(good)) if good else None

    t, q = marker_correlations(y), marker_correlations(p)
    valid = [(i, j) for i in range(9) for j in range(9)
             if t[i][j] is not None and q[i][j] is not None]
    # Undefined correlations are not replaced with zero or silently scored as correct.
    frob = math.sqrt(sum((q[i][j] - t[i][j]) ** 2 for i, j in valid)) if valid else None
    return dict(n=int(len(y)), frobenius=frob, valid_entries=len(valid), total_entries=81,

def fscore(truth, prediction):
    tp = int((truth & prediction).sum())
    fp = int((~truth & prediction).sum())
    fn = int((truth & ~prediction).sum())
    denom = 2 * tp + fp + fn
    return dict(f1=2 * tp / denom if denom else None, tp=tp, fp=fp, fn=fn,
                true_count=int(truth.sum()), predicted_count=int(prediction.sum()))

    return dict(per_marker_r=r, macro_r=average_defined(r.values()),
                vector_rmse_mean=float(rmse.mean()), vector_rmse_median=float(np.median(rmse)),

def knn_impute(train_features, test_features, train_y, mask, k=50, query_chunk=256, reference_chunk=4096):
    \"\"\"Exact Euclidean KNN; both axes chunked. Every marker has its own revealed bank.\"\"\"
    if k < 1:
        raise ValueError('K must be positive.')
    train_features = torch.as_tensor(train_features, dtype=torch.float32)
    test_features = torch.as_tensor(test_features, dtype=torch.float32)
    result = np.empty((len(test_features), 9), np.float32)
    counts = []
    for j in range(9):
        selected = np.flatnonzero(mask[:, j])
        if not len(selected):
            raise ValueError(f'No revealed training neighbours for {MARKERS[j]}')
        kk = min(k, len(selected))
        counts.append(dict(marker=MARKERS[j], bank_size=len(selected), effective_k=kk))
        bank, values = train_features[selected], np.asarray(train_y)[selected, j]
        for start in range(0, len(test_features), query_chunk):
            q = test_features[start:start + query_chunk]
            distances = torch.full((len(q), kk), float('inf'))
            indices = torch.zeros((len(q), kk), dtype=torch.long)
            for ref in range(0, len(bank), reference_chunk):
                b = bank[ref:ref + reference_chunk]
                dist = (q.square().sum(1)[:, None] + b.square().sum(1)[None] - 2 * q @ b.T).clamp_min_(0)
                ids = torch.arange(ref, ref + len(b))[None].expand(len(q), -1)
                combined = torch.cat([distances, dist], 1)
                distances, pos = combined.topk(kk, dim=1, largest=False, sorted=True)
                indices = torch.cat([indices, ids], 1).gather(1, pos)
            result[start:start + len(q), j] = values[indices.numpy()].mean(1)
    return result, counts

def epoch_batches(rows, batch_size, seed, epoch):
    order = np.random.default_rng(np.random.SeedSequence([seed, epoch])).permutation(rows)
    batches = [order[i:i + batch_size] for i in range(0, len(order), batch_size)]

    if len(batches) > 1 and len(batches[-1]) == 1:
        batches[-2] = np.concatenate([batches[-2], batches[-1]])

def loader(pack, rows, args, batches=None):
    # Separate generator: constructing/skipping loaders must not consume augmentation RNG.
    generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(args.seed + 101)

    if batches is None:
        return torch.utils.data.DataLoader(Cells(pack, rows), batch_size=args.bs, **kw)
    # Cells rows are flattened, and batch_sampler indexes that same flattened sequence.
    sizes = [len(b) for b in batches]
    offsets = np.cumsum([0] + sizes)
    sampler = [list(range(offsets[i], offsets[i + 1])) for i in range(len(sizes))]
    return torch.utils.data.DataLoader(Cells(pack, np.concatenate(batches)), batch_sampler=sampler, **kw)

def batch_loss(model, output, ids, targets, masks, pools, pool_masks, raw, calibration, args):
    mu, pp, cov, _ = output
    y = targets[ids].to(args.device)
    mask = masks[ids].to(args.device)
    loss = gaussian_nll(mu, y, cov) if cov is not None else masked_mse(mu.float(), y, mask)
    if pp is not None:
        loss = loss + args.pool_weight * masked_mse(pp.float(), pools[ids].to(args.device),
                                                   pool_masks[ids].to(args.device))
    if model.inverse is not None and args.map_weight:
        # These are the SAME observed single stains, in raw/c coordinates; no extra labels.
        observed_raw = raw[ids].to(args.device)
        map_target = torch.asinh(observed_raw / calibration['c'])
        loss = loss + args.map_weight * masked_mse(model.inverse.transformed(y), map_target, mask)
    return loss


@torch.no_grad()
def validation_loss(model, pack, rows, scale, tensors, calibration, args):
    model.eval()
    total, count = 0., 0
    for x, ids in loader(pack, rows, args):
        with autocast(args):
            output = model(x.to(args.device) / scale)
            loss = batch_loss(model, output, ids, *tensors, calibration, args)
        # Skip cells without any observations (there are none for the supported regimes).
        total += float(loss) * len(x)
        count += len(x)
    return total / count

def predict(model, pack, rows, scale, args):
    model.eval()
    means, features, diagonals, factors = [], [], [], []
    for x, _ in loader(pack, rows, args):
        with autocast(args):
            mu, _, cov, embedding = model(x.to(args.device) / scale)
        means.append(mu.float().cpu().numpy())
        features.append(embedding.float().cpu().numpy())
        if cov is not None:
            diagonals.append(cov[0].cpu().numpy())
            factors.append(cov[1].cpu().numpy())
    return (np.concatenate(means), np.concatenate(features),
            (np.concatenate(diagonals), np.concatenate(factors)) if diagonals else None)

    ap.add_argument('--stop-after-steps', type=int, default=0, help='testing: interrupt after N new steps')
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
    if a.cov_rank and a.regime "'!= '"'full':
        ap.error('--cov-rank 2 requires --regime full')
    for name in ('epochs', 'threads', 'checkpoint_every', 'knn_query_chunk', 'knn_reference_chunk'):
        if getattr(a, name) < 1:
            ap.error(f'{name} must be positive')
    if a.bs < 2:
        ap.error('--bs must be >=2')
    for name in ('seed', 'workers', 'knn_impute', 'max_train', 'max_val', 'max_test', 'stop_after_steps'):
        if getattr(a, name) < 0:
            ap.error(f'{name} must be nonnegative')
    if not np.isfinite(a.lr) or a.lr <= 0:
        ap.error('--lr must be finite and positive')
    for name in ('pool_weight', 'map_weight'):
        if not np.isfinite(getattr(a, name)) or getattr(a, name) < 0:
            ap.error(f'{name} must be finite and nonnegative')

def main(argv=None):

    def subset(rows, limit, stream):

    tr, va, te = subset(tr, args.max_train, 1), subset(va, args.max_val, 2), subset(te, args.max_test, 3)

# N079: new measurements and genuinely joint validation

N079 diagnosis/CSV: composed singles r=.778 versus pooled heads .783 establishes consistency, **not accuracy of separate markers on the same cell**. Test-cell cross-fitting remains diagnostic. K043's b01 replicate discrepancy (.881/.578 for grp:CD45) identifies readout error but no numerical ceiling. N067/N075/N076 close label recycling and all-slide polishing. K033's +.015–.020 per labelled-data doubling motivates new observations.

Gains below are speculative **single-model v10 GOAL deltas versus .6706**, can be zero/negative, and cannot be added to ensemble .6862. Registered gap=.0138; seed SD=.0027. Reserve source FOVs for selection, refit on eligible source rows, then confirm two seeds × two directions with fresh controls (~2 GPU-h per four-run r50 arm). Rebuild the registered ensemble once; promotion bar .6916, ultimate target .70. Preserve v10 common-11, legacy-v5 reporting, inductive exclusion, and no lineage/exclusivity rules. Costs assume one Helma H100; downloads/CPU excluded.

## Common IFC bridge and validation

S-BIAD452: ~98k cells, three donors, nine measured markers/cell (N077/user verification). Audit donor/sample/tube IDs and completeness; partial/unstained tubes cannot supply nine labels. **Only BF1/BF2/SSC enter inference.** Use acquisition compensation, background-subtracted integrated fluorescence, training-donor asinh/scaling. Fluorescence supplies supervision only, including segmentation targets; never fluorescence-derived input masks.

Pixel matching: IFC .25 µm/pixel; BSCCM metadata example .166 ([paper S2](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.06191v1#S2)). Verify release metadata; enlarge IFC by .25/.166≈1.51×, center/pad/crop to 128 (~21.2 µm). Do not shrink by magnification ratio. Match optical bandwidth separately with blur fixed on training/validation donors; compare native IFC resolution. Normalize BF by background transmission and SSC by log1p.

Default **two stems**: IFC three channels; BSCCM 23 LED+phase (SSL-r50 actually consumes 48 with presence planes). Share trunk, retain dataset-specific normalization/affine adapters and assay heads. BF1/BF2 loosely correspond to BSCCM Brightfield; SSC is scatter, not any specific LED darkfield. IFC lacks DPC/phase/angular equivalents. Ablate modality-specific projections into one shared stem with channel/type masks; never replicate SSC into all DF slots.

Map IFC CD14/CD19/CD3/CD45/CD56 to corresponding five BSCCM `single:` targets via shared features and separate assay readouts. CD15/Siglec8/CD4/CD8 remain IFC auxiliaries; CD16/CD123/HLA-DR stay BSCCM-only. Pooled equivalents: gain-adjusted **linear-intensity** CD3+CD19+CD56 before asinh, and CD45→grp:CD45. No IFC equivalent for grp:CD16 or full CD123/HLA-DR/CD14; CD14 alone cannot supervise that pool. Synthetic pools test aggregation, not BSCCM dye calibration.

Joint test: donor A train, B validation, C untouched test; rotate three prespecified folds. Exclude test donor even from SSL/scaling. Predict all nine simultaneously from BF/SSC; report each marker r, macro/worst r, per-cell standardized vector RMSE and profile cosine, plus five-overlap metrics. Compare nine independent regressors at matched capacity/data. Show each donor; bootstrap cells within donor, acknowledging only three biological replicates. BSCCM keeps unchanged GOAL and held-out all-slide pooled metrics; no test-label stacking. Pooled agreement alone cannot validate individual joint decoding.

## Six experiments

**1. Two-stem joint-source r50 — NEW DATA; reverses BSCCM-only training.** Alternate IFC/BSCCM batches, averaging loss by dataset/observed marker. Fully train trunk and assay heads. Adds real joint measurements and ~4,256 B/~3,532 NKT-labelled cells (N077; these are not all pure NK). Expected **+.003–.009**: a hypothetical 50–100% effective data increase gives (.015–.020)×log2(1.5–2)×5/11≈.004–.009; external CD19 .61 versus ours .32–.35 supports headroom, not a transferable ceiling. Cheapest falsifier: donor-held-out IFC pilot plus matched b01 transfer/control, **~2 GPU-h**; stop if IFC predicts CD19 but BSCCM overlap shows no source-validation gain. Build **2 days**. Frozen-probe failure alone cannot reject fine-tuning.

**2. Nine-image fluorescence pretraining — NEW DENSE SUPERVISION.** Train BF/SSC encoder with nine-channel spatial decoder, aligned crops and balanced foreground/background loss; transfer trunk, then fit BSCCM v10 heads. External individual-marker images extend pending N074's six-channel pooled/single BSCCM supervision. Expected **+.002–.008**: +.02 on four outputs would contribute .0073 to the eleven-target mean; N074 supplies no demonstrated gain yet. Cheapest falsifier: coarse 32² decoder versus scalar-only IFC training at matched encoder steps, then b01 transfer/control, **~3 GPU-h**; stop if improved pixels do not improve markers. Build **2–3 days**; reuse N074 alignment logic, not its dataset layout.

**3. Marker-adapted transformer — NEW REPRESENTATION; challenges N053's encoder ranking.** Pretrain DINOv3-S on IFC nine-marker regression using a modality-specific patch embedding; then fine-tune every block on source BSCCM after stem warmup, encoder LR comparable to head LR. N053 already trained all blocks at LR×.1: unfreezing alone is not new. Changes are external marker supervision and physical input adaptation rather than repeated RGB weights. Expected **+0–.008**; failed N053 ViTs and ConvNeXt residual correlations .94–.96 lower confidence. Cheapest falsifier: short external adaptation, matched BSCCM high-LR/×.1 controls, **~4 GPU-h**; stop if neither beats SSL-r50. Build **1–2 days**. N078 separately tests longer in-domain SSL.

**4. Image-conditioned joint uncertainty — NEW JOINT SUPERVISION.** Fit nine means plus rank-2 covariance with marginal MSE and joint Gaussian likelihood on real IFC vectors. No observed marker enters inference; no marker combination is forbidden. Transfer shared features while retaining BSCCM masked scalar heads. Unlike exhausted BSCCM heads, these cells provide measured cross-products. Expected GOAL **+0–.003**; joint likelihood/coverage is the main opportunity because pooled consistency already differs by only .005. Cheapest falsifier: fixed IFC features, diagonal versus rank-2 covariance under donor holdout, **~.3 GPU-h**; stop without held-donor likelihood/coverage gains. Full transfer screen **~2 GPU-h**. Build **1 day**. Report vector RMSE too: better covariance need not improve means.

**5. Distil a 566-angle teacher — NEW MEASUREMENTS; challenges “not image-limited.”** On BSCCM-coherent, synthesize deployed channels with exposure/background correction; teach a paired 24-channel student from all-angle features and pooled labels. Check reconstruction and duplicate cells first. Coherent is **draw 1** ([paper S2](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.06191v1#S2)): permissible only for b1→0, excluded entirely for b0→1. Expected average GOAL **+0–.002**, allowing +.004 in one direction; only 4,304 pooled-labelled cells and N042's low-pass cost ≤.011 make success unlikely. Cheapest falsifier: source-FOV-held-out ridge, all-angle PCA versus synthesized channels, **0 GPU-h**; stop without pooled improvement. Student screen **~1 GPU-h**. Build **2 days**. Teacher improvement must survive distillation.

**6. Hybrid morphology bridge — challenges reliance on deep features alone.** Extract BF cell size/shape/texture and SSC granularity on IFC; compute corresponding BF/DF descriptors on source BSCCM with separate scaling/readouts. Concatenate descriptors with CNN features for measured marker regression, without gates/classes. N077's IFC study reports handcrafted classification balanced accuracy .778 versus CNN .703: representation evidence, not marker-r evidence. Expected **+0–.004**; BF retained 92% of in-domain signal (K014), but SSC/DF equivalence is uncertain. Cheapest falsifier: ridge/boosting hybrid versus CNN features under IFC donor and BSCCM source-FOV holdouts, **~.2 GPU-h** extraction; stop without incremental marker r. Confirm **~1 GPU-h**. Build **1–2 days**.

Order: 1 first; compare 2/3 as representation alternatives; 4 tests joint uncertainty; 6 has a cheap gate; 5 follows its CPU gate. Check pending N074/N078 before overlapping work. Code constraints: `--aux-label` requires identical BSCCM rows, `--init-full` strictly matches all heads, and `--train-panel all` repeats flat N076. External loading/two stems need explicit extensions; preserve source fingerprints and `train_ssl_lf.py --exclude-batch` semantics. No proposed screen exceeds 25 GPU-h.
